target_customer: Managed service providers (MSPs) that want to govern and resell AI to their small business clients.
problem: MSP clients use unmanaged AI tools (shadow AI) and MSPs have no control layer or way to bill for AI usage.
business_model: B2B SaaS for MSPs with usage billing and markup on tokens
product_category: AI governance and agent platform for MSPs

founders.name: Paul Li
founders.background_notes: Described as a three time founder on the YC page.

founders.name: James Jiang
founders.background_notes: Ex Amazon software developer per YC page.

competitors.name: MSPbots
competitors.what: AI and automation dashboards and bots for MSPs

technical_complexity.rationale: Governed workspace, DLP inspection and MCP connectors with RMM and PSA integrations; mostly standard SaaS and proxy engineering.

defensibility.rationale: MSP distribution and integrations help, but MSP platform vendors and AI vendors can add similar governance.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Several MSP tool vendors launched AI features in 2025 and 2026 (Atera, ScalePad, Hatz); no acquisition of MSPilot found.

market_need_then: Company site claims 11 MSP logos as customers; no independent demand evidence found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, benefit focused headlines such as 'Turn Shadow AI into your next revenue line' (company site).

brand_strength.rationale: Name is similar to MSPbots and Pilot.com in search results; no brand press found.

outcome_analysis: MSPilot is a three person Fall 2025 YC company selling an AI control plane to MSPs, from founders with a prior coding assistant that reached 1.5M installs. No funding, exit or distress is verified, and the founders also list OpenBuilder, so the outcome is unknown.
notes: Dealroom lists a 125K seed (unverified, not recorded). Founded year conflicts: YC data launched_at 2023, a directory says 2026; left null. MSPbots source is dated 2023 and only loosely near the batch. The YC page lists OpenBuilder as the founders' current project, so focus may be split.
